subject: Dedicated capacity + isolation: post-call summary & next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@cloudmedsys.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity + isolation — post-call recap (CloudMed)

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key pain points you called out:
- PHI-sensitive inference workloads for clinical-recommendation pipelines (need strict isolation & auditability)
- Current on-prem cluster has high tail latency during peak business hours and unpredictable ops cost
- Procurement & compliance constraints: SOC 2 evidence + KMS integration for keys, and a US-only residency requirement for some datasets

Goals you stated:
- Stable p95 latency target <= 200ms for 1–2k token prompts (primary clinical path)
- Baseline throughput ~50 req/s with bursts to 200 req/s during daily peaks
- Dedicated isolation (customer-only GPU pools) with an SLA for uptime/latency for production endpoints
- Procurement target: PO in Q3; technical pilot in June if possible

Initial sizing and recommendation (high level):
- Start with an 8x A100 reserved pool (dedicated) + config for 4-GPU burst capacity to handle peaks
- Autoscaling and continuous batching to optimize cost while keeping latency SLOs
- SLA: offer 99.95% availability for the dedicated pool; target p95 generation latency of ~150ms under expected traffic after tuning

Deliverables I’ll share by EOD:
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones and owners [Attachment: MAP_CloudMed_20260518.xlsx]
- List of SOC 2 items and evidence we can provide [Attachment: SOC2-evidence-ask.pdf]
- Two pricing scenarios (8 reserved A100s vs 12 reserved A100s) with burst and autoscale modeling

Suggested next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek to validate latency/throughput assumptions and sizing (30–45m) — available slots below.
2) Finance/Procurement touchpoint to confirm PO/contract preferences.
3) Share MAP and pricing scenarios; you review and we iterate.

Proposed times for the Vivek deep-dive (PST):
- Tue 5/19 10:00–10:45am
- Tue 5/19 2:00–2:45pm
- Wed 5/20 9:00–9:45am

Emily — can you confirm which slot works and whether procurement should be on the call?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 (415) 555-0128
[Attachment: MAP_CloudMed_20260518.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: SOC2-evidence-ask.pdf (pdf)]

From: Emily Jones <emily.jones@cloudmedsys.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@cloudmedsys.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + isolation — post-call recap (CloudMed)

Thanks Aisha — this is helpful and matches my notes. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Residency: the primary data for the clinical path must remain in US-East; we may want EU region later but not in initial scope.
- Budget: leadership has signaled a three-tier budget approach for Q3; we’d like cost scenarios (best-effort, recommended, and conservative) so we can take numbers to finance.
- Procurement timeline: PO earliest in early Q3; need to see a clear MAP and a short pilot to validate latency before committing to reserved capacity.

Can you include a comparison table for 8 vs 12 reserved A100s with expected monthly run-rate, burst modeling, and projected token cost per 1M tokens? Also please call out any additional software/observability fees.

I can do Tue 5/19 at 2pm for the technical deep-dive and will invite our lead infra engineer (Mark R.) if that’s OK. Procurement won’t join the 5/19 session but will review the MAP and pricing once we have it.

—Emily
Emily Jones
Head of ML Infrastructure | CloudMed Systems
emily.jones@cloudmedsys.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@cloudmedsys.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + isolation — post-call recap (CloudMed)

Thanks for the invite, Emily — I’ll take the deep-dive and bring a short tech pack. Quick notes so the call is efficient: 

What I’ll cover (15–20m):
- Inference footprint assumptions (sequence lengths, kv cache sizing, expected tokens/req)
- Sizing rationale for 8 vs 12 A100s and the impact on p95 latency under sustained load
- Network isolation options: VPC peering vs Private Link; KMS/HSM integration flow
- Onboarding plan & runbook for a 4–6 week pilot (we’ll include smoke tests for latency and correctness)

Pre-call ask (one item): can you provide an example request/response size (tokens) for the clinical endpoint and a rough QPS distribution (avg vs peak)? That will let me sketch a more accurate burst model for 8 vs 12 GPUs.

I’ll also upload the tech pack to the MAP folder and include a simple cost delta sheet so Aisha can bundle the pricing scenarios.

See you at 2pm PT.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Internal note: bring benchmark numbers for 4k/2k token cases, KV cache settings, and our autoscaler configuration examples]

From: Emily Jones <emily.jones@cloudmedsys.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@cloudmedsys.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + isolation — post-call recap (CloudMed)

Perfect — 2pm works for us. Mark R. (infra) will join to review the isolation/KMS details. Procurement will review the MAP after the call and I’ll flag any PO process items.

I also attached a signed high-level MAP stub so we can lock milestones on our side (we’ll finalize with legal later).

See you shortly.

—Emily
[Attachment: CloudMed_MAP_signed_stub.pdf (pdf)]
